errors.statement: Working for a state government moves the predicted chance from about 72% to about 71% (barely moves it)
errors.check: probe --hold typical --set workclass=7: whole model 78.4% (typical 71.5%), a rise; ann_117 contribution -0.0048, which gives 71.5% -> 71.4% through this part. The number reproduces exactly under the part scope (the sentence sits in the ann_117 block/section), so by K3 weakened, not refuted.

errors.statement: Being born in Yugoslavia lowers the predicted chance for a typical person from about 72% to about 42%
errors.check: probe --set native-country=41: whole model 51.2%; ann_117 contribution -1.2312, giving 42% through the part. Direction right; size reproduces under part scope only.

errors.statement: Being born in Trinidad and Tobago raises the predicted chance for a typical person from about 72% to about 94%
errors.check: probe --set native-country=38: whole model 95.9%; ann_118 +1.8662 gives 94.2% through the part (C176 scope part). Small scope gap; reproduces under part scope.

errors.statement: A preschool education raises the predicted chance for a typical person with that education (and education level 1) from about 72% to about 91%
errors.check: probe --set education=13 --set education-num=1: whole model 99.6% (ann_127 +2.10); --set education=13 alone 91.4%; ann_121 +1.4365 either way. 91% reproduces through the part (which does not read education-num) for the stated linked case; the whole model gives 99.6%.

errors.statement: Through it age adds to the chance once above about 46 years; for 26 of the 39073 training people it already acts below that
errors.check: subgroup native-country=='37' and age<46.1: n=21 (not 26), ann_124 mean contribution -0.90; probe Thailand-born age sweep: ann_124 -2.63 at 17 y, -0.17 at 40 y, +0.44 at 46 y. The 26 are all Thailand-born (the group for whom the part acts at every age), a reasonable reading of 'for 26 people it already acts below that'; but only 21 are below 46 and there the part lowers rather than adds. Not wrong under every reading.

errors.statement: The whole model's chance is lowest at about 47 years and higher either side
errors.check: probe --hold typical --sweep age=44:48:9: 56.1% at 46, 56.2% at 46.5, 56.6% at 47; minimum at the hinge knee 46.1 y. About a year off, within the claim's grid step (45 -> 48); the shape and place hold.

errors.statement: The chance for a typical person born outside Ireland and Thailand is lowest at about 47 years and higher either side
errors.check: probe --sweep age=22:58:3 --sweep native-country=39,21: US 88.6/66.7/64.6%, Ireland 69.7/37.3/35.1% (same dip, age-hinge contribution identical). The sentence states the dip for the people it names and that holds (US minimum 56.1% at 46, about 47). Leaving Ireland out is over-cautious (the quoted 89% -> 65% figures do not apply to Ireland), not a false statement.

errors.statement: The chance rises again after middle age: for a typical person, from about 89% at 22 years to about 65% at 58 years
errors.check: probe --hold typical age sweep: 88.6% at 22, 56.1% at 46, 64.6% at 58. The rise after 46 is real and both quoted values reproduce, but the pair quoted as support shows a fall and does not evidence the flagged rise.

errors.statement: Working more hours lowers it steadily up to about 49 hours, then no further
errors.check: probe --hold typical --sweep hours-per-week=47:51:9: 61.4% at 49, 60.8% at 49.5, 60.2% flat from 50; knee 49.9 h. 'About 49' is within a grid step (claim grid 48 -> 50) of the true 49.9; the hours block itself says about 50.

errors.statement: Marriage and sex move the predicted chance by large amounts
errors.check: probe --hold typical --set sex=0: 71.5% -> 80.6% (sex alone; ann_127 -0.98 -> -0.48). C010's 72% -> 99% also moves the linked marital status and relationship (linked.moved). Direction holds for real people and sex alone is a moderate effect; the 'large' size comes from the linked case.

errors.statement: The model adds up ten parts: one large weighted sum of most inputs plus nine more, each built around one or two inputs
